observations.statement: WM-039 wires notification destination operations to storage, credential custody, live-send authority, delivery, and receipt projection; it wires sound operations to validation, manifests, managed blobs, and local-only preview, and requires provider-specific create/update validation before writing non-secret settings and credential references.

WM-039 requires explicit user action, an enabled destination, masking, rate limiting, and receipt recording for test sends; it also fixes override precedence as built-in, global, project, then runtime safety constraints.

WM-043 classifies three chat Usage command IDs as retired compatibility aliases, prohibits them as canonical production UICommand rows, and requires Usage route/open evidence to preserve OpenSubject and a broad set of correlation fields while targeting usage_event when usage_event_ref is present.

WM-043 uses validator failure plus wiring fixtures as acceptance evidence, including survival of correlation references through dispatch and route restoration and distinction between thread Context Detail Pane commands and app-wide Usage route/open commands.

WM-042 requires production command coverage after exact exclusions, concrete owner-surface locations, removal of bare namespace roots, replacement of fabricated command_applied events, and preservation of projected availability and disabled reasons across the PRD-to-build launch chain.

WM-042 requires commands without persisted domain events to declare no-persist dispatch or route/open receipts with event-test requirements, while launch-chain rows preserve CAS/currentness and receipt or event effects without claiming runtime buildability.

WM-041 routes provider-related onboarding CTAs into provider/account setup with return context, makes skip enter a limited Planning Wizard state without Health readiness, preserves the paid-provider-before-Free-Models sequence and saved order, routes Teacher copy through Assistant Chat, and reuses provider setup from Health/Doctor.

WM-041 acceptance requires every accepted CTA to map to a cataloged command or existing route, forbids false-ready Health state after skip, enumerates allowed return destinations, and requires owner-doc consumption rather than local redefinition.

WM-040 maps the DRY default-guard setting command to storage, emits an update event, refreshes Assistant Chat and run-detail disclosure projections, records receipt provenance for both setting states, and preserves non-DRY authority boundaries when disabled.
WM-040 restricts writes to enabled or disabled_by_user, requires disclosure refresh after a change, and requires the disabled state to remain receipt-backed.

candidate_findings.title: Notification test-send controls lack executable parameters
candidate_findings.statement: WM-039 makes masking, rate limiting, and receipt recording mandatory for test-send wiring but does not specify the fields or representation to mask, the rate-limit key, threshold, or window, the receipt fields and terminal statuses, or the behavior when any control fails.
candidate_findings.impact: Different builders can expose different credential or payload data, enforce incompatible send limits, and produce receipts that cannot serve as a consistent acceptance oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Notification and sound command lifecycle semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: WM-039 maps destination create, update, delete, toggle, and test operations and sound upload, import, delete, restore, export, preview, and mapping operations, but this window does not define operation-specific payload/result contracts, state-transition preconditions, caller authority, idempotency or concurrency behavior, or rollback and partial-failure handling.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can diverge on destructive-operation safety, duplicate sends or writes, restoration semantics, and the consistency of stored settings, credentials, blobs, manifests, and receipts.

candidate_findings.title: Usage correlation requiredness and conflict precedence are undefined
candidate_findings.statement: WM-043 conditions usage_event targeting on usage_event_ref being present and requires many correlation values only where present, but it does not define which fields are required for each command, how malformed or mutually inconsistent references are rejected, or which reference is authoritative when values conflict.
candidate_findings.impact: A route can open the wrong Usage subject, silently discard stronger evidence, or restore a subject inconsistent with the initiating artifact, run, thread, attempt, or receipt.

candidate_findings.title: Usage route restoration lifecycle is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: WM-043 requires correlation references to survive dispatch and route restoration but does not specify persistence lifetime, ordering relative to navigation state, cancellation or back-navigation behavior, stale or deleted targets, retry and deduplication, or a typed failure result.
candidate_findings.impact: Restored routes can lose or reuse stale correlation state and different clients can disagree about whether a failed or repeated open command changes visible navigation.

candidate_findings.title: Retired alias invocation behavior remains ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: WM-043 prohibits retired chat Usage IDs as canonical rows yet permits them to be represented as compatibility aliases or exclusions; it does not state whether an incoming retired ID must be translated, rejected, ignored, or diagnosed, nor what receipt or telemetry proves that outcome.
candidate_findings.impact: Legacy callers can receive inconsistent behavior and an exclusion can hide an invocation path without proving safe migration or an explicit failure.

candidate_findings.title: Persisted-event versus no-persist selection is not deterministic
candidate_findings.statement: WM-042 allows canonical event types or explicit no-persist dispatch and route/open receipts, and calls for event-test requirements, but it does not define the authority or decision rule that selects a path, the required receipt schema and effects, or the exact event-test oracle.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can classify the same command differently, omit a required durable effect, or certify semantically incompatible receipt-only implementations.

candidate_findings.title: Launch-chain CAS and availability state model is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: WM-042 requires launch-chain rows to preserve CAS/currentness, projected availability, disabled reasons, and receipt/event effects, but the window does not define the compared version or token, stale-write result, retry policy, availability states, disabled-reason vocabulary, or projection update ordering.
candidate_findings.impact: Concurrent approvals and stale launch attempts can be handled inconsistently, while the GUI can expose availability or disabled reasons that do not match the accepted command state.

candidate_findings.title: Onboarding CTA-to-command mapping is not exact
candidate_findings.statement: WM-041 says visible CTAs map to an onboarding command family and requires each CTA to map to a cataloged command or existing route, but it does not identify the exact command ID, input, result, or route effect for each CTA in this wiring contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can map the same visible label to different commands or route effects, making first-run behavior and wiring fixtures nondeterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Limited setup state and return context lack a deterministic contract
candidate_findings.statement: WM-041 permits Skip for now to write or reference onboarding_setup_state and describes provider return destinations as appropriate, but it does not define the state or return-context schema, owner and lifetime, destination precedence, resume transition, or behavior for missing, stale, conflicting, or failed return context.
candidate_findings.impact: Skipped or resumed onboarding can route to different surfaces, lose limited-state truth, or incorrectly expose Health readiness depending on implementation choices.

candidate_findings.title: Free Models ordering persistence is not operationally specified
candidate_findings.statement: WM-041 requires the paid-provider-before-Free-Models sequence and saved top-10 order to be preserved but does not define the source of that order, when it is persisted or restored, how changes are reconciled, or how interruption and resume affect sequence state.
candidate_findings.impact: The same user can see reordered models or bypass the intended sequence after refresh, resume, or provider-flow interruption.

candidate_findings.title: DRY setting side effects have no atomicity or failure contract
candidate_findings.statement: WM-040 requires a storage write, event emission, two projection refreshes, and receipt provenance, but it does not define their ordering or atomic boundary, event and receipt payloads, idempotency, concurrent-update handling, rollback, retry, or the visible result when a projection refresh fails.
candidate_findings.impact: Storage, event history, receipts, and GUI disclosures can disagree about whether DRY is enabled, disabled, or successfully applied.

candidate_findings.title: DRY default and mutation authority are unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: WM-040 restricts written values to enabled and disabled_by_user but does not state the initial or missing-value default, migration behavior for other stored values, which actor may mutate the setting, or how simultaneous writes are resolved.
candidate_findings.impact: Fresh, upgraded, and concurrently controlled installations can derive different effective DRY behavior from the same stored or absent state.

candidate_findings.title: DRY disclosure labels are preserved but not bound to outcomes
candidate_findings.statement: WM-040 preserves DRY applied, DRY degraded, and DRY disabled as exact tokens, but this window does not map those visible labels to setting values, runtime outcomes, degraded causes, or projection-refresh failures.
candidate_findings.impact: Assistant Chat and run-detail surfaces can show contradictory trust signals for the same setting and execution outcome.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: WM-039 explicitly requires provider-specific validation before storage or live-send testing, keeps sound preview local-only, and defines override ordering.
WM-039 explicitly prevents quiet or mute behavior from overriding blocked or security-sensitive notifications.

WM-043 explicitly bars retired chat Usage IDs from live canonical production rows, bars generic family-root exclusions from hiding concrete stale rows, and bars receipt-only wiring for route/open effects.
WM-042 explicitly rejects generic Cataloged GUI surface locations, fabricated command_applied events, and bare command namespace roots in production rows.
WM-042 explicitly states that wiring JSON existence is not runtime certification or buildability proof.
WM-041 explicitly prevents skip from producing false-ready Health state, preserves the paid-provider-before-Free-Models order, and routes Teacher behavior through its owner contracts.
WM-041 explicitly bars skip from routing to the dense Home shell by default and bars marking Doctor or Health Ready after provider setup was skipped.
WM-040 explicitly limits setting writes to two values, preserves non-DRY authority boundaries when disabled, and forbids hiding trust-affecting state only in backend logs.

unknowns.statement: Whether WM-039 dependencies define the missing notification command schemas, credential authority rules, rate-limit parameters, receipt contract, and failure semantics cannot be determined from this window.

Whether the current Usage production matrix and exclusion artifact conform to WM-043 is unknown here because the window identifies those implementation surfaces and a future fixture suite but contains no execution result.
Whether the current production wiring matrix and exact exclusion list conform to WM-042 is unknown here because the window names those artifacts and validators but provides no validator output.

Whether the onboarding dependencies and UI Command Catalog fully define exact command payloads, result schemas, and return-context semantics cannot be determined from this window; WM-041 explicitly assigns schema definition outside Wiring_Matrix.
Whether WM-040 dependencies define the DRY event payload, receipt schema, default state, mutation authority, or concurrency behavior cannot be determined from this window.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote:
Notifications and Sounds wiring maps `cmd.settings.open_notifications` to Settings > General > Notifications & Sounds;
  destination create/update/delete/toggle/test commands to notification destination storage, credential custody, live-send
  authority, delivery service, and receipt projection; mapping/override commands to global/project override records; and
  sound preview/upload/pack import/asset delete/asset restore/asset export/mapping set commands to sound asset validation,
  manifest storage, PM-managed blobs, and local-only preview. Destination create/update wiring validates provider-specific
  Slack, Discord, generic webhook, ntfy, Pushover, and Telegram profile payloads against CV-298 before writing non-secret
  settings and credential refs. This PlanUnit records wiring obligations only and does not generate wiring JSON.

acceptance_criteria:
  - Destination test-send wiring requires explicit user action, enabled destination, masking, rate limit, and receipt recording.
  - Provider-specific destination payloads are validated before storage or live-send test wiring can proceed.
  - Sound preview wiring stays local-only and cannot send remote notifications.
  - Global/project override wiring follows built-in < global < project < runtime safety constraints.

negative_constraints:
  - Do not generate wiring JSON, WorkNodes, or executable queues during this compile phase.
  - Do not wire local preview through remote delivery.
  - Do not let quiet/mute override blocked or security-sensitive notifications.

Production wiring for Usage route/open commands consumes UI_Command_Catalog alias metadata. `cmd.chat.open_thread_usage`, `cmd.chat.focus_thread_usage`, and `cmd.chat.close_thread_usage` are retired compatibility aliases and must not appear as canonical production UICommand rows. Wiring evidence for `cmd.nav.open_usage_subject`, `cmd.artifacts.show_in_usage`, and `cmd.artifacts.show_in_ledger` must prove route_open effect_kind, route_target.object_kind = usage_event when usage_event_ref is present, OpenSubject preservation, and correlation passthrough for usage_event_ref, usage_record_id, provider_attempt_ref, attempt_id, node_id, tool_call_id, trace_ref, receipt refs, raw_payload_ref, artifact_id, run_id, thread_id, source_class, source_confidence, source_authority, settlement_status, projection_freshness, and projection_health where present.

acceptance_criteria:
  - validate-wiring-matrix fails if production wiring registers `cmd.chat.open_thread_usage`, `cmd.chat.focus_thread_usage`, or `cmd.chat.close_thread_usage` as canonical command rows instead of compatibility aliases or exclusions.
  - Usage route/open wiring entries declare effect_kind route_open or mixed with route_open detail, not generic receipt-only success.
  - Wiring fixtures prove Usage correlation refs survive dispatch and route restoration without being replaced by timestamp/run/thread/tier filters.
  - Wiring evidence distinguishes thread Context Detail Pane commands from app-wide Usage route/open commands.

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-plans-verify.py validate-wiring-matrix
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
  - future Usage route wiring fixture suite

implementation_surfaces:
  - Plans/Wiring_Matrix.md
  - Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md
  - Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json
  - Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.exclusions.json

negative_constraints:
  - Do not certify retired chat usage IDs as live production UICommands.
  - Do not let generic family-root exclusions hide concrete stale command rows.
  - Do not accept receipt-only wiring for a command whose effect is route/open navigation.

canonical_text: >-
  The FABLE production wiring repair requires the production wiring matrix to cover cataloged UI commands after
  exact exclusions, use concrete owner-surface locations instead of generic Cataloged GUI surface rows, remove
  bare namespace-root production rows, replace fabricated command_applied placeholder events with canonical
  event types or explicit no-persist dispatch and route/open receipts, and keep the PRD Builder to Planning Wizard
  to runtime approval to Plan Compile open-build chain wired with projected availability and disabled reasons.

acceptance_criteria:
  - validate-wiring-matrix passes against the production matrix and exact exclusion list.
  - No production row uses `Cataloged GUI surface` as a concrete location.
  - No production row emits `*.command_applied` placeholder events.
  - Bare command namespace roots are excluded as parser artifacts or compatibility roots, not represented as production UI rows.
  - Commands with no persisted domain event declare explicit no-persist dispatch or route/open receipts and event-test requirements.
  - Launch-chain rows preserve CAS/currentness, projected availability, disabled reasons, and receipt/event effects without claiming runtime buildability.

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-plans-verify.py validate-wiring-matrix
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
  - python3 scripts/pm-plans-verify.py run-gates

implementation_surfaces:
  - Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json
  - Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.exclusions.json
  - Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md
  - future UI command dispatcher fixtures

negative_constraints:
  - Do not treat wiring JSON existence as runtime certification or buildability proof.
  - Do not create runtime handlers, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, or production build tasks.
  - Do not fabricate command_applied events for receipt-only or route/open commands.

canonical_text: >-
  First-run onboarding wiring maps the visible wizard CTAs to the UI_Command_Catalog onboarding command family and
  owner-doc consumers. `Set up a paid provider`, `Use this provider`, `Sign in`, `Set up provider`, and `Reconnect`
  open or resume provider/account setup with return context. `Skip for now` writes or references limited
  `onboarding_setup_state` and opens Planning Wizard in limited setup state without marking Doctor/Health Ready.
  `Review Free Models`, `Maybe later`, and `Continue to Planning Wizard` preserve the paid-provider-before-Free-Models
  sequence and saved top-10 order. `Open Planning Wizard` routes to Planning Wizard as the first full app page after
  setup or skip. The onboarding Teacher copy routes through Assistant Chat/Teacher contracts rather than a separate
  Teacher surface. Health/Doctor `Set up provider` reuses the same provider setup route and return context. This PlanUnit
  records wiring obligations only and does not generate wiring JSON.
depends_on: [F3-411, UCC-106, CV-305, MA-066, MS-122, ACD-431, PWIZ-017]

acceptance_criteria:
  - Every accepted first-run CTA maps to a cataloged UI command or existing Teacher/Planning Wizard route.
  - Skip routing preserves limited setup state and cannot produce a false-ready Health state.
  - Provider setup return context routes back to onboarding, Planning Wizard limited state, Health, or the originating Free Models row/list as appropriate.
  - Free Models review/defer wiring occurs only after the paid-provider prompt.
  - Wiring consumes owner docs rather than redefining provider auth, model readiness, Teacher behavior, or Planning Wizard state.

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
  - future first-run onboarding command wiring fixture
  - future Health provider-setup return-route fixture

negative_constraints:
  - Do not generate wiring JSON, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, or runtime dispatch during this compile phase.
  - Do not route skip to the dense Home shell by default.
  - Do not mark Doctor/Health as Ready when provider setup was skipped.
  - Do not define UICommand payload/result schemas outside UI_Command_Catalog.
  - Do not redefine provider/account readiness or Teacher behavior in Wiring_Matrix.

canonical_text: >-
  DRY Method settings wiring maps `cmd.settings.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard.set` from Settings > General >
  Agent Rules to `app.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard` storage, emits
  `settings.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard.updated`, refreshes Assistant Chat and run-detail DRY disclosure
  projections, and records receipt provenance for enabled and disabled_by_user states. This wiring does not generate
  wiring JSON and does not disable explicit instructions, safety, secrets, source authority, governance, permissions,
  or source-control hygiene when the default DRY guard is turned off.
depends_on: [UCC-104, CV-299, SP-223, ACD-429]

acceptance_criteria:
  - The Settings toggle writes only enabled or disabled_by_user to the DRY default-guard setting.
  - Assistant Chat and run-detail disclosures refresh after the setting changes.
  - Disabled DRY state remains receipt-backed and does not bypass non-DRY authority boundaries.

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
  - DRY Method settings wiring fixture

preserved_exact_tokens:
  - "cmd.settings.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard.set"
  - "app.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard"
  - "enabled"
  - "disabled_by_user"
  - "settings.agent_rules.dry_method_default_guard.updated"
  - "DRY applied"
  - "DRY degraded"
  - "DRY disabled"

negative_constraints:
  - Do not generate wiring JSON, WorkNodes, or executable queues during this compile phase.
  - Do not treat disabled DRY as permission to bypass explicit instructions, safety, secrets, source authority, governance, permissions, or source-control hygiene.
  - Do not hide trust-affecting DRY state in backend logs only.
